column1: # name<TAB>note (known differences between ga68 and a68j; used by tools/rosetta_report.py)

column2: libm: tan of a REAL rounds differently in glibc (tanf) than on the JVM ((float) Math.tan)
libm: sin/ln of REAL values round differently in glibc than on the JVM
evaluation order: in the assignation "IF ... FI := end OF queue := qnode" ga68 (GCC) elaborates the source before the destination, a68j the destination first; Algol 68 leaves the order open

evaluation order: in "ulam[3] := ulam[2] := ulam[1] := one" ga68 checks the bound of the inner assignation first; both stop with a bound error because ga68 ignores the bounds of FLEX [1 : n] CHAR (a ga68 bug that a68j reproduces)
ga68 crashes (segmentation fault): a routine text stored in a heap structure uses a parameter of a procedure that has already returned (no scope check in ga68); a68j keeps the frame alive
ga68 crashes (segmentation fault): procedures that outlive the procedure that created them (ga68 uses GCC nested functions); a68j keeps the frame alive
partial parametrisation (in circle (0, 0, radius, , )), an Algol 68 Genie extension: ga68 compiles the calls with missing arguments and crashes; a68j reports it as unsupported
a row of 2*10^9 BOOL: ga68 crashes (the row is on the stack), a68j runs out of memory (even unboxed as boolean[] the row needs 2 GB, more than the default JVM heap)
the ga68 program was killed (status -9, out of memory: it allocates its rows on the stack); a68j gives the expected result

ga68 crashes (segmentation fault): the logical file end handler is a routine text inside a procedure that has returned when the handler is called; ga68 makes it a GCC nested function with a trampoline in the stack frame of that procedure, and the call jumps into the dead frame. By Algol 68 the call is valid (the routine uses only names of the outer range); a68j runs it
